summary: Zuiei Ito specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University (1980–2013) and lectured at Tokyo, Waseda, and Shinshu universities.
Zuigan Goto was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Second Higher School, the University of Tokyo, and under Sokatsu Shaku. He served as president of Hanazono University in 1932.

Zuiho Yamaguchi specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from the University of Tokyo and studying under Jacques Bacot and Rolf Alfred Stein. He worked at CNRS, Toyo Bunko, the University of Tokyo (1970–1986), and Nagoya University (1986).
Zuiryu Nakamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi in 1944. In 1945, he became a professor in the Department of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University.
Gyurme tubten nyinje studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Pad+ma la studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Édouard Chavannes worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studying at the École Normale Supérieure and under d'Hervey de Saint Denys and Maurice Jametel. He was a professor at the Collège de France (1893–1918) and served with EFEO.

Édouard Huber worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, studying at the Sorbonne, Collège de France, École des Langues Orientales, and under Sylvain Lévi and Johann Baptist Schibenegg. He served at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient from 1901 to 1905.
Élisée Reclus studied at the Faculté libre de théologie protestante de Montauban (1848–1849). He later held a post at the New University of Brussels (~1894–1905).

Émile Benveniste was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Indological studies who studied at EPHE and under Antoine Meillet, Sylvain Lévi, and others. He held chairs at EPHE (1927–1969) and the Collège de France (1937–1969).
Émile Chartier was a philosopher who was educated at the Lycée Pierre-Corneille (~1881–1886) and the École Normale Supérieure (~1889–1892).

Émile Chatelain worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology, having studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1872–1876). He held posts at the École française de Rome (1876–1877) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1881–1925).

Émile Durkheim worked in religious studies and sociology, studying at the École Normale Supérieure and under Wilhelm Wundt. He held academic posts at the University of Bordeaux (1887–1902) and the Sorbonne (~1902–1917).

Émile Senart worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history, studying at Munich and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He held a professorship at the Collège de France and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1908–1928).

Émile-Louis Burnouf worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at the École Normale Supérieure, University of Paris, and under Eugène Burnouf. He was a professor at the University of Nancy (1854–1867) and director of the École française d'Athènes (1867–1875).

Étienne Balazs was a historian and Sinologist who completed his doctorate under Otto Franke (1923–1930). He later served at the CNRS (1949) and held a professorship in Chinese economic history at the University of Paris (~1955–1963).

Étienne Lamotte was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at KU Leuven, Paris, and under Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served as a professor at the Catholic University of Louvain from 1932 to 1973.

Ñāṇavīra Thera worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at Magdalene College and under Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa. He served in the Royal Artillery (1939–1941) and the Intelligence Corps (1941–1945).

Ösel Tendzin was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Fordham University and under Swami Satchidananda Saraswati and Chögyam Trungpa. He served as executive vice president of Vajradhatu beginning in 1973 and succeeded Trungpa in 1987.

Ülo Valk is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tartu (~1981–1986). He held a post at the University of Tartu (~1995) and served as editor of Numen (~2014–2019).
